newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian prince sells family heirlooms for fortune.
newsitem.headline: Italian prince sells family heirlooms for fortune.

text.p: An Italian aristocrat who is cousin to Britain's Prince Charles raised nearly $6 million by selling off family heirlooms from his castle, sale auctioneers said on Monday.

Prince Carlo Alessandro della Torre e Tasso, head of the Italian branch of the German Thurn und Taxis family, sold the contents of his cliff-top Castello di Duino off in a four-day auction which ended at the weekend.

Top items included a large 18th century Venetian carved giltwood bed which Prince Charles once slept in on a visit to the estate on the northern coast of the Adriatic sea, a statement from French auctioneers Beaussant Lefevre said.
The bed went under the auctioneer's hammer for 46 million lire ($27,000), more than five times the estimated price.

The most expensive item among more than 1,500 lots was a late 18th century Neapolitan suite of 12 painted and gilded armchairs, complete with three sofas, which the prince's family used on a regular basis.
The chairs, which had been notified by the state meaning they cannot be exported, fetched 424 million lire after being estimated at 180 to 240 million lire.
A pair of dancing slippers once belonging to Caroline Duchesse de Berry, wife of French king Charles X, sold for one million lire after being valued at half that amount.
The entire sale, which was run jointly by Beaussant Lefevre and Italian house Stadion, fetched 9.91 billion lire or $5.87 million, nearly double the auctioneers' prediction of $3.2 to $4.9 million.
Some 20,000 people from across Europe and the United States came to view the lots, with 500 people attending each day of the sale which was held in the 15th century castle's grounds.

The 44-year-old prince is in the process of selling the property, where his ancestors have lived for the past 400 years, because he says maintaining it has become difficult after the family sold off supporting farms in preceding years.
The family intends to move to one of its other properties in Italy or France.
